questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: Crow, Parrot, Bat, Eagle
questions.explanation: Crow, Parrot, and Eagle are birds. Bat is a mammal (not a bird). Bat is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: Rose, Lotus, Sunflower, Mango
questions.explanation: Rose, Lotus, and Sunflower are all flowers. Mango is a fruit. Mango is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: 14, 21, 28, 36
questions.explanation: 14=7×2, 21=7×3, 28=7×4 — all multiples of 7. 36 is not a multiple of 7 (36=6²). 36 is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: 2, 3, 9, 5
questions.explanation: 2, 3, and 5 are prime numbers. 9 = 3×3, which is a composite number. 9 is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: Iron, Copper, Glass, Aluminium
questions.explanation: Iron, Copper, and Aluminium are metals. Glass is a non-metallic material. Glass is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: Rectangle, Circle, Triangle, Square
questions.explanation: Rectangle, Triangle, and Square are polygons (figures bounded by straight lines). Circle has no straight sides — it is not a polygon. Circle is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Sun
questions.explanation: Mercury, Venus, and Earth are planets in the Solar System. The Sun is a star, not a planet. Sun is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: France, Germany, Italy, Canada
questions.explanation: France, Germany, and Italy are European countries. Canada is in North America. Canada is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: 121, 144, 169, 178
questions.explanation: 121=11², 144=12², 169=13² — all perfect squares. 178 is not a perfect square (13²=169, 14²=196). 178 is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Letter pairs: AZ, BY, CX, DU — find the odd one out.
questions.explanation:
A(1)+Z(26)=27; B(2)+Y(25)=27; C(3)+X(24)=27; D(4)+U(21)=25. All except DU sum to 27. DU is the odd one out.

**Short Trick:** In complementary-letter pairs, the sum of positions should equal 27 (A+Z, B+Y, etc.).
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Letter triplets: BEH, DGJ, FIM, HKN — find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: BEH: B(2),E(5),H(8) — differences +3,+3. DGJ: D(4),G(7),J(10) — +3,+3. HKN: H(8),K(11),N(14) — +3,+3. FIM: F(6),I(9),M(13) — +3,+4. FIM breaks the +3,+3 pattern. FIM is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: 13, 17, 21, 29
questions.explanation: 13, 17, 29 are prime numbers. 21 = 3×7, a composite number. 21 is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: 64, 81, 100, 125
questions.explanation: 64=8², 81=9², 100=10² — all perfect squares. 125=5³ is a perfect cube but NOT a perfect square. 125 is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: Microscope, Telescope, Periscope, Stethoscope
questions.explanation: Microscope, Telescope, and Periscope all use light/optics to observe objects. Stethoscope is an acoustic instrument for listening to sounds (heart, lungs). Stethoscope is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Letter pairs (with gap pattern): AC, EG, IL, MO — find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: AC: A(1),C(3) — gap=2. EG: E(5),G(7) — gap=2. MO: M(13),O(15) — gap=2. IL: I(9),L(12) — gap=3. IL is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: Kidney, Liver, Spleen, Eye
questions.explanation: Kidney, Liver, and Spleen are internal abdominal organs. Eye is an external sense organ. Eye is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: Longitude, Latitude, Altitude, Magnitude
questions.explanation: Longitude, Latitude, and Altitude are geographical/positional measurement terms used to locate points on Earth. Magnitude is a mathematical/physical quantity (size/intensity). Magnitude is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: Honest, Sincere, Truthful, Cunning
questions.explanation: Honest, Sincere, and Truthful are all positive virtues denoting integrity. Cunning means sly or deceitful — a negative trait. Cunning is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: 15, 35, 63, 80
questions.explanation: 15=3×5, 35=5×7, 63=7×9 — all products of consecutive odd integers. 80 is NOT a product of consecutive odd integers (9×11=99, 7×9=63). 80 is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: Chair, Table, Stool, Computer
questions.explanation: Chair, Table, and Stool are items of furniture. Computer is an electronic device. Computer is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Letter groups: BCDE, FGHI, JKLN, PQRS — find the odd one out.
questions.explanation: BCDE: B(2),C(3),D(4),E(5) — consecutive. FGHI: consecutive. PQRS: consecutive. JKLN: J(10),K(11),L(12),N(14) — 'M' is skipped (gap of 2 between L and N). JKLN is NOT consecutive. It is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Numbers: 56, 72, 91, 110 — find the odd one out. [Hint: check products of consecutive integers]
questions.explanation: 56=7×8, 72=8×9, 110=10×11 — products of consecutive integers n×(n+1). 91=7×13, which is NOT a product of two consecutive integers. 91 is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: 4-digit groups: 1256, 2367, 3478, 4590 — find the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: 8, 27, 64, 100
questions.explanation: 8=2³, 27=3³, 64=4³ — all perfect cubes. 100=10² is a perfect square but NOT a perfect cube (4³=64, 5³=125). 100 is the odd one out.
questions.subject: Reasoning

questions.stem: Find the ODD ONE OUT: ACEG, BDFH, JLNP, QRST
questions.explanation: ACEG: A→C→E→G, gap = +2 (alternate letters). BDFH: B→D→F→H, gap = +2 ✓. JLNP: J→L→N→P, gap = +2 ✓. QRST: Q→R→S→T, gap = +1 (consecutive letters, no skip). QRST breaks the alternate-letter pattern. Odd one out: QRST.
questions.subject: Reasoning
